name: Brent safeguarded scalar root solver
definition: Initialize a=left, b=right, c=a, d=e=b−a. Cache f(a), f(b), f(c). Maintain b,c of opposite signs unless f(b)=0; if |f(c)|<|f(b)|, assign (a,b,c)=(old b,old c,old b) with matching values. Let h=(c−b)/2 and τ=2ε|b|+tol/2. Stop if f(b)=0 or |h|≤τ. If |e|≥τ and |f(a)|>|f(b)|, set s=f(b)/f(a). For a=c set P=2hs, Q=1−s; otherwise set u=f(a)/f(c), v=f(b)/f(c), P=s[2hu(u−v)−(b−a)(v−1)], Q=(u−1)(v−1)(s−1). If P>0 negate Q, then P←|P|. Accept interpolation only when Q≠0, 2P<3hQ−|τQ| and P<|eQ/2|, setting e←d and d←P/Q; otherwise set d=e=h. Set a←b and b←b+d if |d|>τ, else b←b+sign(h)τ. Evaluate f(b); if f(b) and f(c) share a nonzero sign, reset c←a, d=e=b−a. Repeat with bounded evaluations.
variables: a,b bracket endpoints; f scalar continuous function; interpolation history
assumptions: Continuous real function on a finite sign-changing interval; check exact endpoint zeros before iteration, positive tol and finite arithmetic; ε is unit roundoff as measured by the cited implementation.
limitations: A sign change does not identify a unique root; discontinuity breaks the existence argument. A small bracket is a location guarantee, not necessarily a small function residual. Floating-point stagnation requires an explicit termination status.
failure_conditions: Invalid initial bracket, nonfinite evaluation, unrepresentable update or exhausted evaluation budget; unsafe interpolation arithmetic must trigger a safe bisection fallback
computation: Cache values and check signs without multiplying function values; guard interpolation denominators and nonfinite trial values, use safe midpoint arithmetic, and report final bracket and residual separately.

source.citation: Forsythe, Malcolm and Moler, Netlib FMM ZEROIN routine, adapted from Brent (1973), initialization, interpolation tests and bracket reset (lines 39–117). https://netlib.org/fmm/zeroin.f

required_inputs: Continuous scalar function, sign-changing bracket and tolerances.
mechanism_note: Uses the ZEROIN form of Brent’s hybrid, with interpolation-history acceptance tests; unlike the existing bisection and secant methods it combines inverse quadratic interpolation and safeguarded fallback. No empirical superiority claimed.

name: Ridders bracketed scalar root solver
definition: Start with ordered endpoints a<b of opposite function signs; return any exact endpoint root. Set m=a+(b−a)/2 and return if f(m)=0. Let D=sqrt(f(m)^2−f(a)f(b)); propose x=m+(m−a)sign(f(a))f(m)/D. Evaluate f(x); if zero return x. From a,m,b choose the nearest point y with sign(f(y)) opposite sign(f(x)); replace (a,b) with sorted (x,y). Repeat until bracket width meets tolerance or budget is exhausted.
variables: a,b bracket; m midpoint; x trial point; f continuous scalar function
assumptions: Continuous real function, strict initial sign change after endpoint-zero checks, finite function values and positive tolerances. In exact arithmetic D>|f(m)|, so x lies strictly inside the original bracket.
limitations: Even-multiplicity roots may lack a sign-changing bracket; finite precision may round a trial onto an existing endpoint. No uniform convergence-rate claim.
failure_conditions: Invalid bracket, nonfinite evaluations, failed representable contraction or exhausted evaluation budget; unsafe correction may be replaced by midpoint sign bracketing
computation: Scale the three function values by their maximum absolute magnitude before forming the radicand; use sign comparisons rather than products to detect opposite signs. Maintain a bracket and report residual and bracket width separately.

source.citation: Brown University, MATHEMATICA tutorial, Bracketing Methods, section III Ridders’ Method (exponential correction formula); MATLAB tutorial Part III, rebracketing rule. https://www.cfm.brown.edu/people/dobrush/am33/python/p3/bracket.html ; https://www.cfm.brown.edu/people/dobrush/am33/Matlab/ch3/bracket.html

required_inputs: Continuous scalar function, sign-changing bracket and tolerances.
mechanism_note: Exponential correction at a midpoint, rather than polynomial inverse interpolation or unguarded secant updates. Under exact arithmetic with opposite endpoint signs the correction magnitude is less than the half-width. The chosen opposite-sign partner retains a bracket no wider than the original half-width.
